speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Welcome. Since you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash, I need to know if the rash appeared immediately after birth or developed a few days later, and whether it is itchy or associated with fever.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and CRP.
REQUEST TEST: Blood culture.

Please describe the appearance of the rash (e.g., vesicles, pustules, macules) and any feeding difficulties you have observed.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules with an erythematous base observed over the trunk and extremities. Palms and soles are spared. Feeding difficulties not observed.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed description; the combination of pustules on an erythematous base with sparing of the palms and soles is highly suggestive. Has the baby developed any fever or shown signs of lethargy since the rash appeared, and did you notice any honey-colored crusts forming? REQUEST TEST: Blood culture and CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin lesion close-up.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Pulse 152/min, Respiratory Rate 51/min; No fever or lethargy observed; Skin lesions described as erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules with an erythematous base over the trunk and extremities, sparing the palms and soles; No honey-colored crusts observed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the classic presentation of pustules on an erythematous base with sparing of the palms and soles, along with the absence of fever or systemic toxicity, the clinical picture strongly points to a specific neonatal condition.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Acne (Verrucous Pustularis).
